prompt.context: Our client, Bailey Brothers, is a retail bank with several branches in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Their main competitor is Potter & Co., a regional bank that also operates in and around the Ann Arbor area. The CEO of Bailey Brothers, George Bailey, would like us to recommend ways to improve overall profitability in the face of an increasingly modernized industry.
prompt.question: How should Bailey Brothers improve its overall profitability? George would like to bring his profit margin to that of Potter's within two years.

clarifying_info.q: What products and services do Bailey Brothers and Potter offer?
clarifying_info.a: Both offer checking, savings, and retirement accounts, as well as mortgages and auto loans, CDs, and investment accounts.

clarifying_info.q: Do both banks have digital capabilities?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, both Bailey Brothers and Potter have well-developed mobile apps and online capabilities.

clarifying_info.q: How many branches does Bailey Brothers have, and is expansion being considered?
clarifying_info.a: Bailey Brothers has eight equally sized branches, has been in Washtenaw County for several decades, and is not considering expanding its footprint at this time.

clarifying_info.q: What is the specific profitability target?
clarifying_info.a: George would like to bring his profit margin to that of Potter's within two years.

exhibits.title: Profit Margin: Bailey vs. Potter (2010–2018)
exhibits.shows: A line chart comparing annual profit margin percentages for Bailey Brothers and Potter & Co. from 2010 to 2018.
exhibits.data: Y-axis: 0%–25% profit margin; X-axis: years 2010–2018; two lines labeled Bailey and Potter showing their respective profit margin trends over time.

exhibits.title: Primary Point of Contact for BB Clients (2010–2018)
exhibits.shows: A stacked or grouped chart showing the breakdown of Bailey Brothers customers' primary point of contact by channel (Website Alone, Mobile App Alone, Website and Mobile) from 2010 to 2018.
exhibits.data: Y-axis: 0%–40%; X-axis: years 2010–2018; three series: Website Alone, Mobile App Alone, Website and Mobile; 2018 data implies 85% of customers interact with Bailey Brothers primarily through online means.

exhibits.title: Income Statements, FY18 (MM)
exhibits.shows: Side-by-side FY2018 income statements for Potter & Co. and Bailey Brothers in millions of dollars, listing revenue, operating expense line items, total operating expenses, and EBITDA.
exhibits.data: Potter: Revenue $400, Salaries and Wages $160, Branch Expenses $48, Marketing $64, Website/App $48, Total Operating Expenses $320, EBITDA $80; Bailey Brothers: Revenue $50, Salaries and Wages $20, Branch Expenses $12, Marketing $8, Website/App $6, Total Operating Expenses $46, EBITDA $4

framework: Revenue levers: new/expanded product offerings, pricing adjustments, growing account balances and customer base
Cost levers: salaries and wages, branch/real estate expenses, marketing spend, technology/app costs
Note: retail banks have largely fixed cost structures (unlike CPG or industrial firms) — variable costs are limited, so cost reduction focus should center on structural fixed costs
Key diagnostic: compare Bailey Brothers' expense structure to Potter & Co. to identify where the gap lies
Given the profitability target is to match Potter's margin, the exact target margin can be read from Exhibit 1

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, what profit margin must Bailey Brothers achieve, and what is the gap versus today?
questions.guidance: Candidate should read Potter's 2018 profit margin from the chart (~20%) and Bailey's current margin. Bailey's current margin: EBITDA $4M / Revenue $50M = 8%. Gap = 20% − 8% = 12 percentage points. Candidate should also note that the two firms had similar margins earlier in the decade and the gap has widened in recent years.

math.setup: Bailey margin = EBITDA / Revenue = $4M / $50M; Potter margin = $80M / $400M
math.answer: Bailey must reach 20% profit margin; current gap is 12 percentage points.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, what trend in customer behavior is visible, and what does it imply for branch strategy?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that online/mobile usage is rising sharply. By 2018, approximately 85% of Bailey Brothers customers interact primarily through online means (Website Alone + Mobile App Alone + Website and Mobile). This implies only ~15% of customers rely primarily on a physical branch. A strong candidate will connect this to the question of whether all 8 branches are necessary.

math.setup: Online primary users ≈ 85% of total customers (implied by 2018 chart data); branch-primary users ≈ 15%
steps: Sum of Website Alone + Mobile App Alone + Website and Mobile in 2018 ≈ 85%
math.answer: 85% of BB customers interact primarily online; only 15% rely on a physical branch.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, compare the expense structures of Bailey Brothers and Potter. Which cost line is disproportionately high for Bailey, and what is the cost-saving solution?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe that every line item for Potter is exactly 8× Bailey Brothers — except Branch Expenses ($48M for Potter vs. $12M for Bailey, a ratio of 4×, not 8×). This signals Bailey has twice as many branches relative to its scale. Reducing from 8 branches to 4 would cut Branch Expenses from $12M to $6M, aligning Bailey's relative expense structure with Potter's. Candidate should then recalculate the new profit margin.

math.setup: Check ratios: Potter / Bailey for each line; then recalculate Bailey income statement with Branch Expenses = $6M
steps: Branch Expenses ratio: $48/$12 = 4× (anomaly — BB has double the branches relative to scale)
Fix: reduce Bailey branches from 8 to 4 → Branch Expenses = $12M / 2 = $6M
math.answer: Closing 4 branches saves $6M, raising Bailey's profit margin from 8% to 20%, matching Potter's target.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks or implementation challenges should Bailey Brothers consider when closing 4 branches?

categories.name: Customer Impact
ideas: Loss of the ~15% of customers who still rely on physical branches
Risk of customer attrition if remaining branches become overcrowded or less accessible
Need to educate offline customers on digital banking capabilities

categories.name: Legal and Lease Obligations
ideas: Longer-term property leases that cannot be exited immediately may delay savings realization
Costs of breaking leases or holding vacant properties
Opportunity to sell owned branch properties as an additional offset

categories.name: People and HR
ideas: Layoffs or role eliminations for branch employees could damage morale and PR
Retraining branch employees for other roles within the bank
Possibility of relocating employees to retained branches or headquarters

categories.name: Operational Continuity
ideas: Which 4 branches to close — optimize for geography to minimize customer inconvenience
Transition planning to migrate customers smoothly to retained branches or online channels
Ensuring retained branches can absorb higher foot traffic from consolidated customer base

recommendation: Bailey Brothers should close 4 of its 8 branches. The physical presence is no longer necessary given that 85% of customers interact primarily online. Closing half the branches will reduce Branch Expenses from $12M to $6M, boosting profit margin from 8% to 20% — meeting George's target of matching Potter's margin within two years.
risks: Loss of the remaining 15% of customers who do not use online resources
Possibility of longer-term leases on branch properties that cannot be exited immediately
PR and morale erosion from layoffs of employees working at the closed branches
next_steps: Further analysis into which 4 branches to close in order to minimize customer impact (geography, usage patterns)
Exploration of leasing contracts and potential to sell owned property assets
Customer education campaign to migrate the remaining 15% of offline customers to digital channels
Retraining, relocating, or providing severance for branch employees affected by closures
